title: MLOps and LLMOps: versioned inputs and rollback
objectives: Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects mlops and llmops: versioned inputs and rollback with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. The shared platform's release artifact contains dataset version, code identity, adapter mode, prompt/index versions and all evaluation results.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: A reproducible AI release links code, dataset, model, tokenizer, prompt, retrieval index, evaluation rubric and environment. MLOps manages training/serving artifacts; LLMOps adds prompt and provider configuration, retrieval and semantic evaluation. Both need experiment tracking and operational monitoring.

A model alias or file named latest is not sufficient provenance. Use immutable revisions and artifact hashes where available, and record provider aliases with observed dates when exact internals are not exposed.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Write a release manifest with all version identities, evaluation run ID, deployment image and rollback target. Register accepted artifacts after gates pass. Track experiments in MLflow or portable JSON with parameters, metrics and artifact locations.

Monitor drift in inputs, accepted accuracy, abstention, latency and cost. Canary a candidate against representative traffic under permissions, then promote only after observing gates. Rollback must restore compatible prompt/model/index/schema versions together.

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A prompt rollback leaves the new incompatible index in place. A training dataset includes future incident resolution fields, causing leakage. A provider alias changes behavior while dashboards show no code deployment.
Test manifest completeness, artifact compatibility, reproducible fixture runs and rollback smoke tests. Preserve old indexes and configuration long enough to perform a real rollback.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: The shared platform's release artifact contains dataset version, code identity, adapter mode, prompt/index versions and all evaluation results. A reader can rerun deterministic fixtures from that record.

SDETs verify that deployment uses the gated artifact and rollback restores the previous contract. Operational drift checks complement pre-release tests because external models and data can change after deployment.

title: Artifact manifests and compatibility-aware rollback
objectives: Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects artifact manifests and compatibility-aware rollback with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Acceptance includes manifest completeness, dataset/case identity, artifact compatibility and observed rollback behavior.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: An experiment's result depends on a compatible set of artifacts. Model, tokenizer, embedding/index contract, prompt, schema, dataset and evaluator versions form a release identity. A mutable latest alias cannot reproduce all of these inputs.

Rollback is a tested operation restoring a compatible set, not a prose instruction to use the old model. Permission revocations and deleted sources must remain enforced even when an older index generation is restored.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Write a manifest after gates pass, linking immutable hashes or revisions and the tested image. Register metrics and artifacts in MLflow or portable JSON. Preserve a rollback target and test a known fixture through that configuration.

Distinguish training artifacts from serving configuration and evaluator configuration. A provider may expose an alias rather than internal weights; record the alias, request date and observed behavior while acknowledging that limit.

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A model rollback retains the new label ordering and swaps categories. A prompt rollback retains an incompatible evidence schema. An older index exposes a document whose access was revoked after the index was built.
Test compatibility before switching traffic and apply current authorization at query time. Keep a manifest completeness check and a rollback smoke case in the release pipeline.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Acceptance includes manifest completeness, dataset/case identity, artifact compatibility and observed rollback behavior. Drift monitoring connects post-release failures to external provider or data changes.

For SDETs, reproducibility claims should be falsifiable: a reader can rerun fixture cases and obtain the same deterministic results from the declared artifact set. Live model repeatability is measured, not assumed.

mistake: A model rollback retains the new label ordering and swaps categories. A prompt rollback retains an incompatible evidence schema. An older index exposes a document whose access was revoked after the index was built.
takeaway: Acceptance includes manifest completeness, dataset/case identity, artifact compatibility and observed rollback behavior.
